newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India buys 720,000/T Feb diesel in tender.
newsitem.headline: India buys 720,000/T Feb diesel in tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) bought by tender 720,000 tonnes of high speed diesel in 17 cargoes for February delivery, traders said on Monday.

They said IOC took three 30,000-tonne cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel for delivery to the Goa or Kandla on the Indian west coast, eight 45,000-tonne cargoes to Kandla, and six 45,000-tonne cargoes to Madras or Haldia on the east coast.

The winners included Swiss trader Glencore with five cargoes, European trader Galaxy with four cargoes, U.S. major Mobil Corp with three cargoes and European major Shell with two cargoes. German trader Mabanaft, Mediterranean trader BB Energy and European major BP won one cargo each.
They said cargoes to Kandla were awarded at between $24.00 and $27.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f).

Cargoes to Goa or Kandla were awarded between $26.00 and $28.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f while east coast cargoes were awarded between $27.00 and $29.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f.
Even though traders last week had anticipated the IOC would buy up to 700,000 tonnes of diesel in the tender, some had been concerned that IOC's February imports would not exceed 500,000 tonnes.
This had led the gas oil swaps to slip from earlier highs.
But traders said that gas oil swaps would rise on Monday with the large import volume.
India had not bought big volumes of diesel in its tenders over recent months.
IOC bought 120,000 tonnes in October, none in November, 520,000 tonnes in December and 345,000 tonnes in January.
